claims.text: A homogeneous amorphous or nanocrystalline lightweight HEA microstructure with pronounced disorder establishes a continuous protective oxide film under high-temperature and corrosive conditions.
Microstructural uniformity simultaneously enhances mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance.
Al–Ti–V–Nb is an example of a lightweight HEA film system that can be synthesized by magnetron sputtering.
The proposed initial Al–Ti–V–Nb film is amorphous or uniformly nanocrystalline and has minimal secondary-phase segregation.
Controlled sputtering or heat treatment can reinforce microstructural homogeneity and optimize lattice distortion.
Less-controlled processing leads to heterogeneous or partially crystallized HEA microstructures.
A uniform, continuous protective oxide layer is necessary to maintain performance at 800–1000 °C and in corrosive environments such as 3.5% NaCl.
A uniform amorphous or nanocrystalline solid solution minimizes local compositional fluctuations and defect concentrations.
Minimizing local compositional fluctuations and defect concentrations promotes formation of a continuous, self-healing oxide layer.
Lattice distortion and chemical disorder impede dislocation motion and crack initiation.
A homogeneous, chemically disordered microstructure facilitates rapid formation of a protective oxide film.
The protective oxide film lowers the diffusivity of oxygen and corrosive ions.
Lower oxygen and corrosive-ion diffusivity preserves mechanical integrity and surface passivation during extreme environmental exposure.
The homogeneous processed alloy will have higher compressive strength than the heterogeneous baseline alloy.
The homogeneous processed alloy will have lower corrosion current density than the heterogeneous baseline alloy.
The homogeneous processed alloy will exhibit less oxidation mass gain over time than the heterogeneous baseline alloy.
If temperature or corrosive severity exceeds the stability limits of the passivating oxide, the benefit of microstructural homogeneity will diminish.
The magnitude of strength, corrosion, and oxidation improvements depends on alloy composition and processing.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis applies pronounced lattice distortion as a strengthening mechanism to an amorphous-or-nanocrystalline state. Conventional lattice distortion presupposes a crystal lattice, so its application to the amorphous branch is conceptually inconsistent unless reformulated as local atomic-packing distortion.
